lines: כִּי הוּא אֵל גָּדוֹל וְנִשְׂגָּב מְאֹד

review: The hymn is Psalm 95 and 100 sung as a procession: 1:1–8 is Ps 95:1 (נָרִיעָה לְצוּר יִשְׁעֵנוּ) with Ps 100:2, 2:1–8 Ps 95:3–5 (אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ הַיָּם וְהוּא עָשָׂהוּ) with Ps 24:1–2, and 3:1–8 Ps 95:6–7 (נִכְרְעָה וְנִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה … וְהוּא רֹעֵנוּ) nearly verbatim.

The refrains are not identical across the stanzas, because the printed Arabic is not: stanza 1 repeats مرنمين مرنمين / مرنمين هاتفين, while stanzas 2–3 change the first refrain to غنوا له مرنمين. The Hebrew renders the first with זַמְּרוּ לֵאלֹהִים, זַמֵּרוּ (Ps 47:7) and keeps the second constant, so the difference of the print survives.

1:3 צוּר יִשְׁעֵנוּ, אֲדוֹן הַפְּדוּת — the Arabic صَخْرِ الْخَلَاصِ وَرَبِّ الْفِدَا is Ps 95:1's צוּר יִשְׁעֵנוּ; the Hebrew keeps the verse's construct and adds אֲדוֹן הַפְּדוּת for the second half of the Arabic, since a bare repetition of 'rock' would lose the redemption the stanza is celebrating.

3:5 הוּא אֵל, וַאֲנַחְנוּ עֲבָדָיו — the Arabic فَهُوَ الْإِلَهُ وَنَحْنُ الْعَبِيد is the Ps 95:7 relation; the Hebrew keeps the stark verbless clause and the word עֲבָדִים, because the stanza's comfort depends on the distance the next line closes with עַמּוֹ.

3:7 יִרְעֶה צֹאנוֹ — the Arabic يَرْعَى الْقَطِيعَ uses the flock-word; the Hebrew uses צֹאן, the word of Ps 95:7 and 100:3 (עַם מַרְעִיתוֹ וְצֹאן יָדוֹ), so the line quotes the psalm's own pastoral noun rather than a later synonym.
